phrase.zh: 沿着轨迹多看一步，熟悉的世界便多了一种可能。
phrase.en: Follow a trace one step further, and the familiar world gains another possibility.

visual.zh: 深绿场中一条灰银薄板水平贯穿中央，一条象牙轨迹由左下浅弧穿板，再以更紧的弧线向左回转至上边缘；稀疏小点随线分布，左侧留白。薄板细排线与中性黑白版保持同一关系。
visual.en: A silver-gray horizontal plate spans a deep-green field. One ivory trail rises from a shallow lower-left arc through the plate, then turns more tightly leftward toward the top; sparse dots follow it, with quiet space at left. Fine hatch models the plate; neutral monochrome retains the geometry.

background.zh:
安德森因发现正电子，与赫斯分享1936年诺贝尔物理学奖，两人各获一半。1932年，他研究雾室里的粒子轨迹，发现一种质量接近电子、电荷却相反的粒子。轨迹穿过铅片后弯曲程度的变化，帮助判断粒子的运动方向。画面把这一观察关系化为一条穿板后弯曲更明显的细线，是原创定性寓意，没有真实实验的尺寸、磁场方向或测量数值；短句为原创。
1936年物理学奖；获得本年度奖项的一半。获奖理由（中文译述）：发现正电子
background.en:
Anderson shared the 1936 Nobel Prize in Physics with Hess, each receiving half, for discovering the positron. In 1932 he studied cloud-chamber tracks and identified a particle close to electron mass with opposite charge. The change in curvature after crossing a lead plate helped establish its direction of motion. A fine path curving more tightly after the plate is an original qualitative metaphor, without actual apparatus dimensions, magnetic-field direction or measurement values. The phrase is original.
1936 — The Nobel Prize in Physics. Received half of the prize. Official motivation: for his discovery of the positron
